input.quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
input.rationale: Garman owns all IP in the Work, expressly including the Improvements and the Schedule "D" Modifications developed for Sparkling, and the only licence back (Section 2) is a non-transferable, location-limited licence to "use" the Software and Documentation, with additional fees payable for other locations and Section 3(c) prohibiting sublicensing. That fails the fallback: our licence to the deliverables is not perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide or royalty-free and carries no right to modify or sublicense for our business. There is also no limit on Garman's use of Sparkling's converted data. We therefore target the fallback (Garman keeps ownership of its software and know-how under Section 13) by broadening the Section 2 grant, conforming the Section 3(c) sublicence restriction, and limiting Garman's use of our data to processing solely to provide the services. We note the licence term remains subject to the Section 17 termination mechanics, which we address under the termination rule rather than duplicating here.

proposal.summary: Make Sparkling's licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free with modify/sublicense rights; conform sublicence restriction; limit Garman's use of Sparkling's data
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Garman owns all IP in the Work including the Modifications built for us (Section 13), so we need at least a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense for our business, and we conform Section 3(c) so that permitted sublicensing is not separately prohibited. We also limit Garman's use of our data to processing it solely to provide the services; Garman's ownership of its own software is unaffected.
